examples.en: The brain uses glucose as energy.
I got a glucose injection at the hospital.
Glucose is found in fruit and honey.

examples.ko: 피곤할 때 포도당 사탕을 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people eat glucose candy when they're tired.

examples.ko: 피 속 포도당이 너무 높으면 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If the glucose in your blood is too high, you should go to the hospital.

examples.ko: 혈당 검사는 피 속 포도당 양을 재는 거예요.
examples.en: A blood sugar test measures the amount of glucose in your blood.

explain: 일상에서 '당'은 단맛 나는 것 전체를 말하고, 포도당은 그중 몸이 에너지로 쓰는 한 종류예요. 병원에서는 포도당이 든 수액을 놓고, 피 속 포도당 수치는 '혈당'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I was weak, so I got a glucose injection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in hospital settings.

phrases.en: The nurse changed my glucose IV drip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 링거처럼 혈관으로 넣는 포도당 액체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is glucose liquid given through an IV drip.

phrases.example: 포도당이 부족하면 머리가 잘 안 돌아가요.
phrases.en: If you lack glucose, your brain doesn't work well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 에너지가 모자란 상황을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain when the body is short of energy.

explain_en: In daily life 당 refers to sweet things in general, and 포도당 is the one kind your body uses for energy. Hospitals give 수액 containing 포도당, and the glucose level in blood is called 혈당.

examples.en: I put smoked salmon in the salad.
Dad bought smoked duck.
This shop has a good smoky aroma.

examples.ko: 훈제로 만든 고기는 오래 보관할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Smoked meat can be stored for a long time.

examples.ko: 훈제 맛이 강해서 아이는 잘 안 먹어요.
examples.en: The smoked flavor is strong, so the child doesn't eat it much.
I like raw salmon more than smoked.

explain: 음식 이름 앞에 붙여서 '훈제 오리', '훈제 연어', '훈제 치킨'처럼 말해요. 연기로 맛을 낸 음식이라서 '구이', '튀김'과 요리 방법이 달라요. 포장에 '훈제'라고만 쓰여 있는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.en: I ordered smoked chicken on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '훈제' 뒤에 음식 이름을 붙여요. 연기로 맛을 낸 닭고기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a food name after '훈제'. Chicken flavored with smoke.

phrases.en: I put a smoked egg in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연기로 향을 낸 달걀이에요. 간식으로 많이 먹어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An egg flavored with smoke, often eaten as a snack.

phrases.en: Smoked pork belly has a rich aroma, so it's delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연기로 맛을 낸 삼겹살이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pork belly flavored with smoke.

explain_en: It goes in front of a food name, as in 훈제 오리, 훈제 연어, and 훈제 치킨. The food is flavored with smoke, so the cooking method differs from 구이 or 튀김. Packages often say just 훈제.

examples.en: The long journey of preparing for the Olympics has finally begun.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 전국 투어 대장정을 마치고 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: The singer came back after finishing a long nationwide tour.

examples.ko: 십 년간의 대장정 끝에 책이 완성됐어요.
examples.en: After a ten-year-long effort, the book was completed.
The players set out on the long road toward the championship.
This long journey was really long and hard.
We safely finished the long journey that was shooting the film.

explain: 실제 먼 길뿐 아니라 오래 걸리고 힘든 큰 일이나 프로젝트를 비유할 때 많이 써요. '대장정에 오르다/나서다', '대장정을 마치다'처럼 짝지어 쓰고, 가벼운 여행에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 새 앨범 제작의 대장정에 올랐어요.
phrases.en: Our team set out on the long journey of making a new album.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 힘든 일을 시작할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for starting a big, difficult undertaking.
phrases.en_equiv: set out on a long journey

phrases.en: I graduated after finishing a three-year epic journey.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 걸린 일이 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a long, demanding task is finished.

phrases.en: After a long journey, I achieved my dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻의 쉬운 말로, 오래 걸린 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, similar phrase for a long process.

explain_en: Long, difficult undertaking or trek; figurative, dramatic, often written (대장정을 마치다) Besides a literal long trek, it is often used figuratively for a big, long, demanding project. It pairs with '대장정에 오르다/나서다' and '대장정을 마치다', and it is not used for a light trip.

examples.en: The new business has finally gotten on track.

examples.ko: 공사가 본궤도에 오르려면 시간이 더 걸려요.
examples.en: It will take more time for construction to get properly on track.
The economy is slowly returning to its normal course.
The project has settled onto its track, so I feel relieved.
It will take time for the economy to get back on track.
I put the derailed schedule back on track.

explain: '본궤도에 오르다/들어서다'처럼 거의 정해진 모양으로 써요. 시작 단계를 지나 일이 안정적으로 잘 굴러간다는 뜻이에요. 비슷하게 '궤도에 오르다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: The new shop is finally on track.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 안정적으로 잘 굴러가기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things start running smoothly.

phrases.en: The project has finally got on track.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오르다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 시작 단계를 지났다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '오르다', suggesting the start phase is over.
phrases.en_equiv: to move onto the main track

phrases.en: The business is on track, so I'm relieved.
phrases.nuance_ko: '본'을 뺀 모양이에요. 말할 때 더 짧게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form without '본', which is shorter in speech.

explain_en: It is used almost only in set forms like '본궤도에 오르다/들어서다'. It means a matter has passed the starting stage and is running steadily. People also say '궤도에 오르다' in a similar way.

t90.ax: I put the derailed schedule back on track.

examples.en: On the downhill road, the bike zooms along.
The wind is whistling hard, so it's really cold.
Cars whiz by on the highway.

examples.ko: 아이가 눈 위에서 씽씽 썰매를 타요.
examples.en: The child zips along on a sled over the snow.
I read a book on the speeding train.
A motorcycle whizzed past me.

explain: 무언가가 빠르게 달리거나 바람이 세게 불 때 쓰는 말이에요. '쌩쌩'과 느낌이 비슷해요. 속도가 시원스럽게 빠르다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Cars whiz by on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 옆을 스쳐 가는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for something rushing past you quickly.

phrases.en: I rode a bus speeding along the highway.
phrases.nuance_ko: '씽씽' 뒤에 '달리는'을 붙여 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put '달리는' after it to describe a noun.

phrases.en: Motorcycles zoom past.
phrases.nuance_ko: '씽씽'과 거의 같지만 조금 더 센 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as '씽씽' but a bit stronger.

explain_en: It is used for something moving fast or wind blowing strongly. The feel is similar to '쌩쌩'. It carries a sense of brisk, refreshing speed.

examples.en: The front wheel of my bicycle went flat.
The front wheel was wobbling, so I went to the repair shop.
I replaced the motorcycle's front wheel with a new one.
The trick of riding with the front wheel up is difficult.
The car's front wheel fell into a puddle hole.
The front tire is badly worn.

explain: 앞쪽에 달린 바퀴이고 반대말은 '뒷바퀴'예요. 소리는 [압빠퀴]로 나니까 소리 나는 대로 쓰지 않도록 조심하세요. 자전거, 오토바이, 자동차 이야기에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I replaced both the front and rear wheels with new ones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '뒷바퀴'와 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the word with its opposite, rear wheel.

phrases.en: The front tire got a flat, so I walked here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자전거나 차 바퀴에 문제가 생겼을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a bike or car tire has a problem.

phrases.en: I checked the car's front wheels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자전거 말고 다른 탈것에 붙여서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can attach other vehicles to the word, not only bicycles.

explain_en: It is the wheel at the front, and the opposite is '뒷바퀴'. It is pronounced [압빠퀴], so be careful not to spell it as it sounds. It often comes up when talking about bicycles, motorcycles and cars.

en: amusement park; recreation area; pleasure ground

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the amusement park with my family.
There is a bike path in the riverside recreation area.
I bought cotton candy at the entrance of the recreation area.
That recreation park has pretty cherry blossoms in spring.
Old amusement parks had many small rides.
There are many restaurants near the recreation area, so it's convenient.

explain: 놀이기구가 있는 '놀이공원'이나 '놀이동산'보다 더 넓은 말이에요. 강가나 바닷가, 공원에 놀이기구와 식당이 있는 오래된 나들이 장소에 어울려요. 요즘은 '놀이공원'이라는 말이 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: We ate a packed lunch at the recreation park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유원지에서 한 일을 말할 때 '에서'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에서 to say what you did at the park.

phrases.en: I met my friend at the entrance of the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when naming a meeting place.

phrases.en: I took a walk at the seaside recreation park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유원지가 어디에 있는지 앞에 붙여 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put the location before the word to say where the park is.

explain_en: Outdoor leisure spot, often by river or lake; rides optional. This is a broader word than 놀이공원 or 놀이동산. It suits older outing spots by rivers, seas or parks with rides and restaurants. These days 놀이공원 is the more common word.

examples.en: The team arrived safely in Beijing yesterday.
When the army entered the city, people cheered.

examples.ko: 대표팀은 내일 경기가 열리는 도시에 입성해요.
examples.en: The national team arrives tomorrow in the city hosting the match.

examples.ko: 새 감독이 오늘 팀에 입성할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The new coach is set to join the team today.

examples.ko: 서울에 입성하는 날 비가 많이 왔어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot on the day I arrived in Seoul.

examples.ko: 시골에서 올라온 청년이 대도시에 입성하고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The young man who came up from the countryside was stunned on arriving in the big city.

explain: 성이나 도시 안으로 들어서는 큰 장면에 어울리는 말이에요. 요즘은 뉴스에서 선수단이나 가수가 새 도시나 팀에 도착할 때 많이 써요. 행사장 안으로 들어갈 때는 '입장하다'를 써서 쓰임이 달라요.

phrases.en: The team is about to enter the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 어떤 곳에 들어갈 때 쓰는 짝말로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for being about to enter a place, common in news.

phrases.en: As soon as he entered the city, he went to his lodging.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어선 바로 뒤에 다른 일이 이어질 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for something that happens right after entering.

phrases.en: The news spread that the king had entered the castle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 들어왔다는 소식을 전할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when passing on news that someone has made an entrance.

explain_en: Entering a big city or arena, often with achievement (본선에 입성하다) It fits a big scene of entering a walled city or capital. In today's news it's used when a team or singer arrives in a new city or joins a new team. For going into an event venue, use 입장하다 instead.

examples.ko: 지역 문화의 고유성을 지키는 일이 중요해요.
examples.en: Protecting the uniqueness of local culture is important.
Hangeul is a script with outstanding uniqueness.
We made the product while keeping the brand's distinct identity.

examples.ko: 전통 음식의 고유성이 점점 사라지고 있어요.
examples.en: The distinctive character of traditional food is gradually disappearing.
When translated, the distinctiveness of this phrase is lost.
Each country has a different kind of uniqueness in its language.

explain: '독창성'은 새롭게 만들어낸 것에 쓰고, '고유성'은 원래부터 그것만이 가진 특징에 써요. '고유성을 지키다', '고유성을 살리다', '고유성을 잃다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 우리는 전통 음식의 고유성을 지키고 싶어요.
phrases.en: We want to protect the uniqueness of traditional food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 가진 특징을 그대로 보호한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means protecting the original character as it is.

phrases.example: 이 건물은 옛 모습의 고유성을 살려서 고쳤어요.
phrases.en: This building was restored while keeping its original character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특징이 잘 보이게 한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like making the distinctive character stand out.

phrases.en: The village lost its uniqueness as it became a tourist spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래의 특징이 사라졌다는 아쉬움을 담아 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said with regret that the original character is gone.

explain_en: '독창성' is for something newly created, while '고유성' is for a trait that something has had all along. Common phrases are '고유성을 지키다', '고유성을 살리다', and '고유성을 잃다'.

examples.en: This car is small, so it is easy to maneuver.
I cut down my luggage to be more mobile.

examples.ko: 기동성 때문에 사람들이 스쿠터를 많이 타요.
examples.en: People ride scooters a lot because of their mobility.
Laptops are portable, but the screen is small.
At the site, safety comes before mobility.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 가벼워서 기동성에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: This bag is light, so it helps with getting around.

explain: '기동력'과 비슷해서 서로 바꿔 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 차, 가방, 노트북처럼 가볍고 움직이기 편한 것을 말할 때도 나와요. '기동성이 좋다/떨어지다/높다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: With lots of luggage, your mobility drops.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이기 불편해질 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving around becomes harder.

phrases.en: This laptop is light, so it is very portable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 가볍고 들고 다니기 편하다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praises something light and easy to carry.

phrases.en: Mobility matters for fire trucks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기동성'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with 기동성.

explain_en: It is close to '기동력' and the two are often swapped. It also comes up for things that are light and easy to move, like cars, bags and laptops. People say '기동성이 좋다/떨어지다/높다'.

t90.ax: I cut down my luggage to be more mobile.

en: to be astute; to be shrewd

examples.en: He responded quickly and prevented an accident.
Thanks to a quick, sharp judgment, we reduced the loss.
A cat's movements are really nimble.

examples.ko: 저는 행동이 기민하지 않아서 늘 한발 늦어요.
examples.en: I'm not quick to act, so I'm always a step behind.

examples.ko: 점원이 기민했던 덕분에 손님이 오래 기다리지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the clerk's alertness, the customer didn't have to wait long.
In a crisis, you need to be quick and also calm.

explain: 상황을 재빨리 알아채고 알맞게 움직인다는 느낌이에요. '빠르다'는 속도 자체를 말하고, '민첩하다'는 몸놀림이 빠르다는 쪽이 강해요. '기민하다'는 판단과 대처가 빠를 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The firefighters moved swiftly and put out the fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황을 보고 재빨리 알맞게 행동한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means acting quickly and appropriately after reading the situation.

phrases.example: 판단이 기민하지 않으면 좋은 기회를 놓쳐요.
phrases.en: If your judgment isn't quick, you miss good opportunities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 대처가 느리다는 뜻을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says someone's response is slow.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 몸이 민첩해서 공을 잘 잡아요.
phrases.en: That player is agile, so he catches the ball well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기민하다'가 판단과 대처가 빠르다면 '민첩하다'는 몸놀림이 빠르다는 쪽이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 기민하다 is quick judgment, 민첩하다 leans toward quick body movement.

explain_en: It carries the feel of noticing a situation quickly and acting appropriately. '빠르다' is about speed itself, and '민첩하다' leans toward quick body movement. '기민하다' fits best when judgment and response are fast.

examples.en: It was a presentation that showed the new employee's spirit.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어도 기백을 잃지 않고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to keep my spirit even as I get older.
A spirited young man stepped forward.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 기백에 눌려서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was overwhelmed by his spirit and couldn't say a word.

examples.ko: 기백으로 가득한 응원 소리가 경기장에 울렸어요.
examples.en: Cheers full of spirit rang through the stadium.

examples.ko: 목소리는 작아도 기백만은 누구한테도 지지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if my voice is small, I'm second to none in spirit.

explain: '패기'와 비슷하게 굽히지 않는 씩씩한 마음과 태도를 말해요. '기백이 있다/넘치다'처럼 쓰고, 목소리나 표정에서 느껴지는 힘을 칭찬할 때 어울려요.

phrases.en: That young man seems to have spirit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씩씩하고 굽히지 않는 사람에게 쓰는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praise for someone bold who does not back down.

phrases.en: His speech was full of spirit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 아주 많이 느껴진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a strong sense of energy is felt.

phrases.en: I envy the boldness of young people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기백'과 비슷하고, 젊은 사람에게 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 기백, used more for young people.

explain_en: Like '패기', it means a bold, unyielding spirit and attitude. People say '기백이 있다/넘치다', and it suits praise for strength felt in a voice or expression.

examples.en: By my own measure, I did my best.

examples.ko: 자기 깜냥도 모르고 큰 일을 맡으려고 해요.
examples.en: He wants to take on a big job without knowing his own limits.

examples.ko: 그 일은 내 깜냥으로는 해결하기 어려워요.
examples.en: That problem is hard to solve with my abilities.

examples.ko: 깜냥이 안 되는 일은 욕심내지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't be greedy about things beyond your capacity.

examples.ko: 그는 자기 깜냥을 넘는 자리에 올라서 힘들어해요.
examples.en: He rose to a position beyond his capacity and is struggling.

examples.ko: 깜냥만큼만 하면 되니까 너무 걱정하지 마요.
examples.en: Just do as much as you can, so don't worry too much.

explain: '능력'은 어디에나 쓰지만 '깜냥'은 '제 깜냥에는', '깜냥이 안 되다'처럼 굳어진 말투로 자주 써요. 한계를 말하거나 겸손하게 말할 때 나오고, '깜냥이 뛰어나다'처럼 칭찬에는 잘 안 써요. 윗사람에게 '제 깜냥에는'이라고 하면 겸손하게 들려요.

phrases.example: 그 일은 제 깜냥이 안 돼서 못 하겠어요.
phrases.en: That job is beyond my ability, so I can't do it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력이 부족해서 감당하기 어렵다고 말할 때 써요. 겸손하게 거절할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you lack the ability to handle something. It can also be a modest way to decline.

phrases.example: 처음에는 제 깜냥에 맞는 일부터 시작할게요.
phrases.en: At first I'll start with work that suits my ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 능력에 맞는 정도를 말할 때 써요. '맞는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that matches one's ability. You can use '맞는' to modify a noun.

phrases.example: 자기 깜냥을 알고 무리하지 않는 게 중요해요.
phrases.en: It's important to know your limits and not overreach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 능력의 한계를 안다는 뜻이에요. 충고하는 말에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means knowing the limits of your ability. Often appears in advice.

explain_en: '능력' fits almost any context, but '깜냥' mostly appears in set phrases like '제 깜냥에는' and '깜냥이 안 되다'. It is used to state limits or to sound modest, and rarely for praise, as in '깜냥이 뛰어나다'. Saying '제 깜냥에는' to a superior sounds humble.

t90.ax: By my own measure, I did my best.

en: to be strong; to be firm; to be steadfast

examples.ko: 태풍에도 꿋꿋하게 서 있는 나무가 멋있어요.
examples.en: The tree standing firm even in the typhoon looks great.
Grandmother protected the family with her unshaken strength.
He is a resilient child who gets right back up even when he falls.

examples.ko: 친구들은 저를 꿋꿋하다고 하지만 사실 많이 힘들어요.
examples.en: My friends say I am strong, but actually I am having a hard time.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 꿋꿋하니까 걱정 안 해도 돼요.
examples.en: That friend is strong, so you don't need to worry.

examples.ko: 늘 꿋꿋하던 형이 오늘은 눈물을 보였어요.
examples.en: My older brother, who was always steady, showed tears today.

explain: '강하다'는 힘이 센 느낌이 있지만, '꿋꿋하다'는 힘든 일 앞에서도 마음이 흔들리지 않는 모습에 써요. '꿋꿋하게 버티다, 살아가다, 견디다'처럼 '-게' 형태로 동사와 잘 어울리고, '꿋꿋이'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I held on firmly even in a hard situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 때 흔들리지 않고 견딘다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means enduring without wavering in hard times.

phrases.en: He firmly walked his own path.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿋꿋하게'와 뜻이 같고 부사로 바로 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '꿋꿋하게', used directly as an adverb.

phrases.example: 그녀는 힘든 일 앞에서도 꿋꿋한 태도를 보였어요.
phrases.en: She showed a steadfast attitude even in the face of hardship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔들림 없이 굳센 태도나 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an unshaken, steadfast attitude.

explain_en: Strong in spirit — stays firm through hardship. '강하다' suggests physical strength, but '꿋꿋하다' describes someone whose heart does not waver even in hard times. It pairs well with verbs in the '-게' form, as in '꿋꿋하게 버티다/살아가다/견디다', and you can also say '꿋꿋이'.

t90.ax: That friend is strong, so you don't need to worry.

en: to be persistent; to be tenacious; to be stubborn

examples.en: That person keeps calling persistently.
After persistent effort, I finally passed.
The reporter kept asking questions doggedly.
I laughed at the puppy that kept tagging along.

examples.ko: 그의 끈덕진 성격 덕분에 일이 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to his tenacious character, the work got done.
If you're tenacious, good results will come someday.

explain: 포기하지 않고 끈질기게 계속하는 모습이에요. 비슷한 말로 '끈질기다'가 있고, 상대가 귀찮아할 만큼 계속할 때도 쓸 수 있어요. '끈덕지게'처럼 부사형으로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The detective persistently chased the criminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끈덕지다'와 비슷하고 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '끈덕지다' and used more often.

phrases.en: Reporters keep tailing that actor relentlessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀찮을 만큼 계속 따라다닐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone follows so persistently it becomes annoying.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 정말 끈덕져요. 절대 포기하지 않아요.
phrases.en: That friend is really tenacious. He never gives up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 말할 때 쓰는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form used to describe a person's character.

explain_en: Sticky, stubborn persistence, as with a pushy salesperson. It describes continuing without giving up. A similar word is '끈질기다', and it can also be used when someone keeps going to the point of being annoying. It often appears in the adverb form '끈덕지게'.
